 (By Shri Shankar Bansal, Learned Counsel 
 Respondent [R-3].
 )
 Th is appeal coming on for hearing this day, t h e court
 following:
 Order

The instant Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 29.10.2011 passed in Claim Case No.92/2011 by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Vidisha, whereby the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.4,22,000/- in favour of appellants/claimants along with interest @ 6% per annum.

2. The facts necessary for disposal of the present appeal in brief are that on 6.2.2011 at about 12:00 noon Sukhnandan Sehariya by sitting on backside of bicycle driven by Virendra was going to his village from Vishanpura.

At that juncture near peekclon chaurah driver of Bolero Jeep No.MP-15-CA1740 by driving the said jeep rashly and negligently dashed the bicycle from behind,
due to which, Sukhnandan Sehariya sustained grievous injury and died on the spot.

3 . Learned counsel for the appellants submits that learned Tribunal has not awarded the future prospects at the rate of 40% on the amount of loss of dependency as well as the amount of compensation towards conventional head is on lower side.
It ought to be Rs.70,000/- instead of Rs.17,000/-.; therefore, it has been prayed that the award is to be enhanced in that proportion.

4. Per contra, the learned counsel of the Insurance Company opposed the prayer on the ground that appropriate award has been passed in favour of the claimants/appellants and there is no ground for enhancement of the award and it has been prayed that the appeal may be dismissed.
5.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and after perusal of the record, it is found that learned tribunal has assessed the loss of dependency as Rs.4,05,000/- as per para-13 of the impugned award but has not awarded future prospect @ 40% considering the age of the deceased.

It is also revealed from the para-14 and 15 of the impugned award that only Rs.17,000/- has been awarded towards conventional head while it ought to be Rs. 70,000/- as per the dictum of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi 2017 (16) SCC 680.
6.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi 2017 (16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having considered the future prospects and amount of conventional head, the future prospect @
40% comes to Rs1,62,000/- and the amount on conventional is also may be enhanced by Rs.53,000/-.

but since the appellant have filed this M.A. for enhancement of two lakhs; therefore,
the enhancement may be restricted to Rs.2,00,000/-
7.
In the result, Rs.2,00,000/- is hereby enhanced in favour of the appellant in addition to the award already passed in his favour.
The remaining terms and conditions as stipulated in the impugned award shall remain intact.
8. With the aforesaid observation, the Miscellaneous Appeal is disposed off.
